title: Amazon Main Image Rules at Scale | AIVideosUGC
description: Meet Amazon's main-image rules with one pure-white setup for the whole catalog. Keep the product large, check the corners, then send the files.
h1: Amazon Main Image Rules for Every Listing
eyebrow: Pure White for the Main Image
lead: Meet Amazon's main-image rules at catalog scale. One pure-white setup, then send the set to Seller Central.
summary: One white setup covers the whole catalog, not just the first color. The square stays white, the product stays large, and the frame stays limited to what the box contains.

sections.h2: A Pure White Main Image for Every Product
paras: Amazon requires a pure white main image. If the corners are not white, the listing can drop out of search until you replace that picture.
Take one backpack photo as an example. Remove the old background, then set the corners to pure white, 255 on red, green, and blue. You do not need a studio for that.
Sale stickers, badges, and extra objects stay off this picture. The product should fill most of the square, and it should be the one you ship.
sections.alt: Olive canvas backpack centered on a pure white background.

paras: A shop with many products can reuse the white square once the first one looks right. Save that setup and apply it to the rest.
Use that same white square as the first photo on your own store too.
You set pure white once, choose how much of the square the product fills, and name what ships in the box. The next product uses that setup.
You confirm shape, color, and label against the item in your hand, and then you publish the file that matches.

sections.h2: Start From a Phone Photo, Not a Studio
paras: You do not need a white studio. The phone photo needs the whole product, sharp, with even light and a little space around every edge.
Take the photo near a window, on a plain surface, and hold the phone at the product's height. Show what the buyer finds in the box. Flash can blow out the color, so window light is safer.
sections.alt: Adult hand holds an olive canvas backpack upright beside a bright window.

sections.h2: Make the Pure White Main Image
paras: Open the [AI product background changer](page:change-background) or the [AI product photo generator](page:photo-hub). Ask for the product on pure white, filling most of the square.
Then sample a corner. It should read 255 on red, green, and blue. If it does not, ask again before you upload.
sections.alt: Olive canvas backpack on a pure white background.

sections.h2: Use the Same White Setup on Every Product
paras: A white main image keeps a listing easy to find in search. Replace a gray main image and the listing can show in search again. The later photos are not the ones this rule is about.
Once the first square is right, use that same square on the next color. The API is not a separate install. It can start the next file from the catalog you already keep.

sections.h2: Keep Your Brand on the Later Images
paras: Save your colors and your wordmark for the photos after the main image. Those later photos are where colors and the wordmark belong. The main image stays a clean product on white, with no lettering.

The white square is only the first picture. The product in use, or a hand for scale, belongs in the later spots. [Photos of daily use](page:lifestyle-photos) and [photos with a person](page:model-photos) cover those spots.

sections.h2: How to Make Amazon Listing Photos in 3 Simple Steps
paras: Upload your product photo. Get the main image right on one product before you touch the rest. The square is white, and every piece that ships is in the frame.
Describe your scene for the later pictures. The second picture can show the product in use. Add your colors in the editor only on that later image.
Download and post. When that pair looks right, repeat it for the other products and send the files to Seller Central.

sections.h2: How a Catalog Seller Uses the Main Image
paras: Every new product gets the same pure-white main image. Photos of the product in use stay in the later image spots.

sections.h2: Check the Product Before You Upload
paras: You upload a file whose corners are full white and whose product matches the one in your hand. Check the corners with a color picker, then set the real item next to the screen.

Each corner should be pure white, with no gray haze. Zoom in on labels, because small lettering is where a new image often goes wrong. If the words are wrong, try again from a sharper phone photo before the file goes to Seller Central.
sections.alt: Adult hands compare an olive canvas backpack with a blank white square card.

sections.h2: When the Product Is White, Clear, or a Set
paras: Set the product's shape first, light the edges, and show exactly how many pieces the listing sells.

Side light keeps a pale product's outline visible on white. Take the starting photo with light from one side, and mention that side light in the line you type. If two pieces ship, both stay in the frame. A clear bottle needs the same edge light, or it can disappear into the white.
sections.alt: Adult hand shapes an olive canvas backpack upright on a white backdrop.

sections.h2: Keep White for the Main Image Only
paras: Only the first picture has to be the white square. Picture two can show the product in use. Picture three can show a detail up close.
Make the pictures first, then add any words in the editor. [Photos of daily use](page:lifestyle-photos) are for those later spots. A soft shadow, when you want one, stays off the main image.

faq.q: What if the product is white, clear, or a set?
faq.a: Use side lighting to keep a white or clear product visible against pure white. Include every item in a set that you actually ship.
The image should keep your product’s original shape and color. Review straps, labels, and edges against your source photo before posting.

faq.q: How many credits does one white image use?
faq.a: One white-background image costs 24 credits. Failed jobs return their credits. Starter costs $24.50 monthly for 200 credits, Pro costs $35 for 300, and Premium costs $63 for 600.

faq.q: How can I make an Amazon image with a pure white background?
faq.a: Upload a phone photo, remove its background, and choose pure white. Check the product edges and every corner before using it as a main image.

faq.q: Can my shop system start the white image?
faq.a: Yes. Your shop software can send product photos through the API and request white-background images. Review the results before adding them to listings.

faq.q: Can an image made here be my Amazon main image?
faq.a: Yes, if the image shows the product you sell on pure white without extra props or text. Check Amazon’s current main-image rules before uploading.

faq.q: Can I make white-background images for many products?
faq.a: Yes. Apply the same white background and framing to multiple product photos. Review each image so the color, label, and shape still match the item you sell.

faq.q: What happens if my Amazon main image breaks the rules?
faq.a: Amazon may suppress a listing with a noncompliant main image. Replace it with a clear product image on pure white, then check that the listing is visible again.

faq.q: What are Amazon’s main image requirements?
faq.a: Amazon main images need a pure white background, a clear view of the product, and no extra text or props. Check the current rules for your category before uploading.

faq.q: Why does my white background look gray on Amazon?
faq.a: It may be off-white or have a gray shadow near an edge. Check that the background is RGB 255, 255, 255 across the full image.
